blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Performance reviews can be stressful — but they do not have to be. A good review is never a surprise. It is the natural conclusion of the small conversations that happen throughout the year, so nothing in the meeting should catch either side off guard.

In the meeting, the manager shares honest feedback: what went well, what needs to improve, and what goals come next. But the employee also speaks — about challenges faced, the support they need, and where they hope their career is going. A review is a conversation, not a monologue.

The real value comes later. HR often collects the main points and follows up: what was agreed, what will be measured, and when to check progress again. Without that follow-up, even the most honest conversation quietly fades, and the same issues return next year.

items.q: According to the text, why should a good review never be a surprise?
options: Because the goals are always the same
Because HR reads the notes in advance
Because it follows small conversations held all year
items.why: "the natural conclusion of the small conversations that happen throughout the year".

items.q: What does the manager share in the meeting?
options: What went well, what needs to improve, and what goals come next
The results of an anonymous survey
items.why: "what went well, what needs to improve, and what goals come next."

items.q: The text says a review is "a conversation, not a monologue." This suggests that…
options: only HR should lead the meeting
the employee should also speak and be heard
items.why: Inferência: se não é monólogo, ambos falam — o funcionário fala de desafios, apoio e aspirações.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Follow-up is where much of the value lies.
A review with no follow-up still solves the problem.
Feedback should be honest and specific.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que sem follow-up a conversa 'quietly fades' e os problemas voltam.

items.q: What can we infer will happen if HR does not follow up?
options: The employee will be promoted anyway
The same issues are likely to return the next year
items.why: Inferência: "the same issues return next year" — sem acompanhamento, nada muda de fato.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie enquanto ela passa a limpo as anotações de uma avaliação. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me write these notes up while the review is still fresh in my mind. I'll use reported speech so it reads as a clean summary rather than a transcript.

So, on the positive side, Daniel said he was proud of the way the team had handled the migration project. He told me the launch had gone more smoothly than he expected, and he acknowledged that his colleague Priya had carried a lot of the load.

Then we moved on to the areas of improvement. He admitted that his written reports were sometimes too long, and he said he would try to keep them shorter and clearer. I noted that as a concrete action, not just a good intention.

On his aspirations, he explained that he wanted to move into a team-lead role within a year or so. We agreed a stretch goal around that — he committed to mentoring a junior analyst next quarter.

Finally, the follow-up. I'll send the development plan by Friday, and we'll check progress again in three months. If I don't diarise that now, it simply won't happen.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is Sophie writing the notes up straight away?
options: Because HR requires it within the hour
Because the review is still fresh in her mind
items.why: "let me write these notes up while the review is still fresh in my mind."

items.q: What did Daniel say about the migration project?
options: That the launch had gone more smoothly than he expected
That it had failed to launch
That he had done it alone
items.why: "the launch had gone more smoothly than he expected", e ele reconheceu a ajuda de Priya.

items.q: What concrete action did Daniel commit to regarding his reports?
options: To ask Priya to write them
To keep them shorter and clearer
items.why: "he said he would try to keep them shorter and clearer" — anotado como ação concreta.

items.q: Why does Sophie say the follow-up "simply won't happen" if she doesn't diarise it now?
options: Because follow-up is easy to forget once the meeting is over
items.why: Inferência: sem marcar na agenda, o acompanhamento se perde — o valor está justamente nele.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's approach to the notes?
items.why: Inferência: ela cobre pontos fortes, melhorias, aspirações e follow-up, com ações concretas.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Each manager will appraise their team members twice a year." To appraise means to…
items.why: To appraise = avaliar formalmente o desempenho.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We turned her feedback into a ___ with clear, measurable actions."
items.why: Development plan = plano de desenvolvimento, que transforma feedback em ações concretas.

items.q: "Doubling the client base this year is a real stretch goal." A stretch goal is…
options: an ambitious target that pushes you to grow
a target that is easy to reach
a goal set by HR only
items.why: Stretch goal = meta ambiciosa, que empurra além da zona de conforto.

items.q: "Before criticising, she took time to acknowledge his effort." To acknowledge means to…
items.why: To acknowledge = reconhecer — reconhecer o trabalho antes do feedback gera confiança.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He has a strong ___ of delivering projects on time."
items.why: Track record = histórico comprovado de resultados.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem numa avaliação de desempenho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "HR will follow up on the agreed actions next month." To follow up means to…
options: check progress and take the next step
items.why: To follow up = dar sequência, acompanhar o que foi combinado.

items.q: "She kept the feedback constructive rather than personal." Constructive feedback…
items.why: Constructive = construtivo: aponta melhorias de forma útil, não ataca a pessoa.

items.q: "Daniel committed to mentoring a junior analyst next quarter." To commit to something means to…
items.why: To commit to = se comprometer firmemente a fazer algo.

items.q: "His main area of improvement is time management." This expression refers to…
items.why: Area of improvement = ponto de melhoria — onde a pessoa precisa evoluir.

items.q: "Let's not just agree in the room — we need to follow through." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado, não parar no acordo verbal.
